name: optuna-continuous-demo
notes: The CONTINUOUS half of the docs/24 §8 search seam: optuna-search.json's twin, differing only in the shape of `space`. Here clip.lo is a range spec — {"low", "high"} plus the optional "log"/"int" flags — so the seeded TPE sampler draws a real-valued threshold instead of picking from a list. Reach for this form whenever the knob is genuinely continuous (a learning rate, a threshold, a regularization weight): a list would force you to guess the resolution up front, and hpo-grid REFUSES range specs because exhaustive enumeration over an interval is meaningless. The planner checks only that the space keys address existing params of ancestors of the objective; the range grammar itself belongs to OptunaSearch (dskit/pipeline/libs/optuna.py:_spec_problems), which is why this document needs the optuna extra to run but plans without it. Every `uses` is an import reference, so it runs against the bare toolkit with zero registrations: python -m dskit.pipeline run examples/pipeline/optuna-continuous.json --asof 2026-01-01

clip.notes: clip.lo is the tuned knob; the value here is the base-pass default the search overrides — overrides address EXISTING params only

validate.notes: the objective's source: a score node reading 'val' — selection never sees test (spec §8)

search.notes: the range spec: low/high are REQUIRED finite numbers with low < high; add "log": true for scale-free knobs (needs low > 0) and "int": true for integer knobs (integer bounds). A degenerate range is a one-value categorical — write it as a list. 8 trials is the whole budget: unlike a grid there is nothing to enumerate, so n_trials alone decides how long the search runs.

report.notes: downstream of the search: consumes the winner pass
